ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Customer due diligence and beneficial ownership profiling are governed by the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18938, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree; the Act on Prevention of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction; the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality; the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and its Enforcement Decree; the Commercial Act (Articles 287 through 328) for Yuhan Hoesa; and FATF Recommendation 24. Beneficial ownership data is reported to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy/KOTRA, while the public commercial register does not disclose the natural-person UBO chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry of the foreign investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the document in the origin state; if the origin state is a Hague Apostille Convention member, obtain an Apostille from that state's designated competent authority; thereafter use the sworn Korean translation. Do not add consular legalization. If the origin state is not an Apostille member, notarize the document and then legalize it exclusively at the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that non-member state. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Corporate Existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry, ministry of justice, or equivalent statutory authority in the foreign investor's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize in the origin state and obtain an Apostille from the origin state's Hague Apostille competent authority when applicable; otherwise use consular legalization through the Korean Embassy or Consulate in the non-member state. Never chain Apostille and consular legalization together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney appointing the local incorporator and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent managing body of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute the resolution or power of attorney before a notary public; authenticate by Apostille if the origin state is an Apostille Convention member; if the origin state is not a member, perform consular legalization at the competent Korean diplomatic mission. Use only one route.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Memorandum and Articles of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official corporate records of the foreign investor or its registered company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy from the originating registry, notarized, then authenticated exclusively by Apostille or consular legalization depending on the origin state's Hague membership. No sequential combination of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign investor and its principal shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The foreign investor's relationship bank or financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issue on bank letterhead, sign by authorized bank officer, notarize the signature, and authenticate by Apostille or consular legalization solely according to the non-member or member status of the issuing bank's country.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of address of each shareholder and natural-person beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuance authority or notary public in the owner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certify the copy before a notary; add an Apostille for Hague member states or consular legalization for non-member states as the single applicable route.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Korean-language Articles of Association for the Yuhan Hoesa being formed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Local notarization only; no Apostille or consular legalization is required because this instrument is produced for direct filing with the Korean court registry.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any incorporation step, screen every shareholder, member, director, officer, authorized signatory, and ultimate beneficial owner holding at least 25 percent of equity against OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU and UK consolidated sanctions to the extent relevant, and the Republic of Korea consolidated sanctions list maintained under the Act on Prevention of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction. Conduct Politically Exposed Person screening using domestic and international PEP databases, adverse-media checks, and financial institution watchlists. Apply fuzzy matching for transliterated Korean and foreign names, verify passport identity by notarized copies, trace the full ownership chain to natural persons, document the source of funds, and record all screening evidence in a conflict-free compliance file retained for at least seven years. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any deposed or serving senior government official, foreign PEP, or sanctioned-related link. Suspicious results must be filed with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit immediately and before any corporate registration proceeds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (I-REGiS) of the Supreme Court of Korea at www.iros.go.kr and the commercial registry division of the competent district court in the intended registered office locale
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Korean Commercial Act and related registration rules, the company name must be in Hangul script and the corporate form suffix must be Yuhan Hoesa for this limited liability company. The four-tier naming convention is: first, the distinctive/fanciful element; second, the business-object descriptor; third, the statutory legal form suffix; and fourth, an auxiliary English or romanized transliteration. Foreign-language words are permitted only where transliterated phonetically into Hangul and accompanied by the original spelling. An English-only name is not registrable; the English name Yuhan Hoesa LLC is treated as an auxiliary trade name and must be supported by the registered Korean name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry judge rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written objection with the same registry office within 14 days, attaching evidence of distinctiveness, the corrected four-tier Korean name, and, if necessary, the written consent of any conflicting registered holder. If the objection is dismissed, the applicant may appeal the registration decision to the district court within 14 days. A final negative determination may be challenged through administrative litigation before the competent administrative court within 30 days. During the appeal the applicant should prepare an alternative name and may resubmit immediately once the ambiguity is cured.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or mail-forwarding street address is not permissible as the sole registered office for a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in retail FPV drone sales. The National Tax Service requires a physical place of business for the issuance of Korean tax invoices, VAT registration, and business registration; banks require an active physical presence and on-site due diligence before opening a corporate account under the Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act. For this business, customs, after-sale returns, liability, and drone-related consumer protection further require inventory handling capability. A serviced office or coworking suite with a dedicated lease, visible company signage, meeting rooms, staff presence, and documented operational substance may satisfy the statutory mandate. A detached post box or virtual office without an actual workplace on the lease will be rejected and may trigger enhanced monitoring by the tax authority, bank, PayPal, and Stripe.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection risk is quantified as moderate-high, approximately 40 percent within the first 12 months of operation. Checklist: lease in the company name; match between registry address and site; exterior and interior signage; accessible staff; inventory and storage for drone parts; accounting books; VAT invoices; customs declarations; records of carbon-fiber milling and brushless motor integration; bank statements; and compliance with applicable drone radio-frequency, remote ID, and safety marking rules. Municipal tax offices and the National Tax Service may inspect under the Local Tax Act and Framework Act on National Taxes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000 as extensively amended), specifically Articles 287-2 to 287-74 governing the Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa); Article 289 (contents of articles of incorporation); Article 292 (notarization of articles); Article 293 (paid-in capital); Articles 542-2 to 542-13 (external audit thresholds for certain balance-sheet sizes); and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident investors. The corporate form is a Korean limited liability company having legal personality distinct from its members, with each member's liability limited to the amount of the member's subscribed contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the competent District Court (Beopwon-dung-gi-gwa). For a registered office in Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office; for other locations, the District Court Registration Office of the local court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), filed in the prescribed court registration form and accompanied by the notarized articles of incorporation, certificate of capital deposit, minutes or written consent of incorporators, acceptance declarations of directors and auditor, and proof of the registered office lease or ownership.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. The incorporators may fix paid-in capital at any lawful amount, and no escrow or blocked account is mandated by statute. However, the full subscribed capital must be deposited into a domestic bank account held in the name of the company or the incorporators before the incorporation registration, and a certificate of capital deposit certified by the bank must be submitted to the court. For a carbon-fiber milling and FPV racing drone assembly company, paid-up capital of at least KRW 100,000,000 (approximately USD 75,000) is commercially recommended to satisfy banking due diligence, supplier credit limits, factory lease underwriting, and foreign-invested enterprise registration with Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), if applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHANG HOESA, A KOREAN LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY

WHEREAS, the Company, Yuhan Hoesa, is being incorporated as a limited liability company under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; and

WHEREAS, the incorporators have subscribed for the entire authorized capital and have caused the first meeting of the Board of Directors to be convened for the purpose of fixing the corporate governance framework, banking arrangements, registered office, and statutory officers; and

WHEREAS, the directors have determined that the resolutions below are necessary and proper to complete the statutory organization of the Company and to enable it to lawfully commence the business of carbon-fiber milling, brushless motor integration, assembly, and sale of FPV racing and hobby drones;

NOW, THEREFORE, upon motion duly made, seconded, and unanimously adopted by the directors present, the following resolutions are hereby approved and declared effective as of the date first written above:

1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. That the issued and paid-up share capital of the Company shall be KRW 100,000,000, divided into 20,000 shares, each with a par value of KRW 5,000. Each foundational shareholder has subscribed for and paid in full in cash the shares allocated to such shareholder, as shown in the subscription schedule and the certificate of capital deposit issued by a licensed domestic bank. The Board hereby ratifies all subscriptions, share allocations, and payments made to date and directs the Representative Director to deposit the aggregate paid-in capital into the designated corporate capital account and to preserve the certificate of capital deposit for filing with the registration court.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. That Shinhan Bank, Seoul Corporate Banking Division, is hereby approved as the Company's primary domestic banking institution, and the PayPal and Stripe payment rails are approved as the standard retail remittance channels for online export sales of the Company's drone products. The Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer are each authorized to act as single signing officers on the corporate bank accounts, provided that any disbursement exceeding KRW 30,000,000 shall require the joint signature of the Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer, or alternatively the joint signature of two other directors designated by the Board.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE. That the registered office of the Company is hereby fixed at [Insert Full Street Address, City, Republic of Korea], within the registration jurisdiction of the Seoul Central District Court. The Representative Director is authorized to execute and deliver the lease or acquisition instruments, to file the statutory registration notices with the court registry, tax authority, and Korea Customs Service, and to affix the corporate seal in connection with all such filings.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. That [Name of Director A] be and hereby is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Company; [Name of Director B] be appointed Chief Financial Officer and Director; and [Name of Director C] be appointed Statutory Auditor. Each such officer is authorized, jointly or severally within the limits of their statutory authority, to execute contracts, open bank accounts, obtain the Factory Establishment Permit, environmental registrations, civil defense fire safety certificates, and KC product safety approvals necessary for the Company's FPV racing drone manufacturing operations.

5. GENERAL. That the Board determines that all actions lawfully taken by any incorporator, director, or officer prior to the date of this resolution are confirmed and ratified, and that the Representative Director, together with the Statutory Auditor where required by law, is authorized to sign and file any documents, make any declarations, pay any fees, and take any steps necessary to give full effect to the foregoing resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution, and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean notary public, with subsequent filing before the Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must prepare articles of incorporation in compliance with the Korean Commercial Act for a Yuhan Hoesa. The articles must state the legal name as Yuhan Hoesa, the purpose clause covering carbon-fiber milling, brushless motor integration, FPV racing and hobby drone assembly, wholesale and retail sale, and the export of such products; the total stated capital; the par value and number of shares; the exact registered office address; the number of directors and the manner of representation; and the duration and dissolution terms. Each incorporator must execute the articles in duplicate, mark and initial all amendments, and appear before a Korean notary public to confirm legal capacity and signing authenticity. The notary will issue a notarization certificate. If any incorporator is a foreign national or foreign legal entity, a passport or apostilled corporate certificate and a sworn English-Korean translation of non-Korean documents must be provided before notarization.
required_dossiers: Notarized original articles of incorporation in duplicate
Minutes of the incorporation meeting or unanimous written consent of incorporators
Passports or national identification copies of all incorporators and directors
Power of attorney, apostilled corporate registration certificate, and sworn translation for any foreign corporate member
Proposed registered office address confirmation and consent of the building owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or reviewing authority requests corrections, execute amended pages and re-notarize the revised articles. If the court considers the corporate purpose misleading or incompatible with the Commercial Act, amend the purpose clause by unanimous incorporator consent and resubmit the notarized revised articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Pre-Registration Bank Account and Deposit of Paid-In Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea authorized under the Banking Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional domestic bank account in the tentative name of the company or the incorporators before the court registration. The incorporators or the designated director must deposit the full amount of the stated paid-in capital into that account, either by wire transfer from the account of each subscriber or by cash deposit, clearly recording each subscriber's name and share allocation. The bank must issue a certificate of capital deposit expressly stating the amount paid, date of deposit, depositor identity, beneficiary legal entity, and account number. This certificate must be current on or shortly before the date of court filing, generally not older than two weeks. The account is unrestricted but should not be drawn down before incorporation registration. The deposit and the certificate create the capital proof required by the court for incorporation registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of capital deposit issued by the bank
Bank transfer confirmations or deposit slips for each subscriber
Subscriber list with share allocations and amounts
Tentative articles of incorporation
Identification documents of the depositor and company representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open an account in the tentative corporate name, open the account in the name of the representative director as trustee and convert the account to the corporate name immediately after registration. If the capital certificate becomes stale, request an updated certificate from the bank and align the certificate date with the registration filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation and Corporate Seal at the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the competent District Court, for Seoul the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office, and for other municipalities the court with territorial jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization and capital deposit, file the statutory application for registration of incorporation with the District Court Registration Office. The application must be signed by the representative director or a duly authorized agent and submitted with the notarized articles of incorporation, the certificate of capital deposit, written acceptance declarations from each director and the statutory auditor, the incorporation minutes, and proof of registered office. The court will examine the application under the Commercial Act and the Framework Act on Registration, Notarization and E-Government. Upon approval, the court assigns a corporate registration number and issues a certificate of registered matters. The company must then complete the corporate seal registration with the same office, submitting a specimen seal and the representative director’s identification. Fees are paid by revenue stamps or electronic payment method designated by the court.
required_dossiers: Completed application for registration of incorporation
Certified copy of notarized articles of incorporation
Certificate of capital deposit
Minutes of the incorporators' meeting or written resolution
Written acceptance declarations of all directors and the statutory auditor
Power of attorney if filing through an agent
Registered office lease agreement or ownership certificate
Identity document of the representative director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order, cure each stated defect within the prescribed period, typically 10 to 14 days, and resubmit the corrected documents. If the court rejects the capital certificate, deposit any shortfall and obtain a corrected certificate. If the registered office address is not accepted, amend the articles and lease to a valid address and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Account Activation with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), competent local district tax office (Se-mu-seo) having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after incorporation registration, apply to the district tax office for a corporate business registration certificate under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act. Submit the corporate registration certificate, certified copy of the articles of incorporation, identity of the representative director, lease contract, bank certificate, and corporate seal certificate. The tax office will issue a business registration certificate containing a unique ten-digit business registration number. The company must then register for electronic tax invoice issuance, corporate income tax, value-added tax, withholding tax, and employer social insurance reporting. If the company exports drones, it must also register with Korea Customs Service for export clearance and obtain an EPC (Export/Import) number, using the same corporate address and registration documentation.
required_dossiers: Corporate business registration application form
Corporate registration certificate issued by the court
Certified copy of the articles of incorporation
Registered office lease or building ownership certificate
Representative director identification and photo ID
Bank account confirmation and seal certificate
Corporate seal specimen
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office delays issuance because court records are not yet synchronized, obtain a certified copy of registered matters from the court and submit it personally to the tax office. If the application is returned, provide the missing lease or corporate documents and re-apply using the NTS Home Tax Service online portal or in-person window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Factory Establishment Permit and Site Safety Approval for Physical Manufacturing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal government (Si/Gun/Gu) and the Korea Industrial Complex Corporation (KICOX) under the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the company will perform carbon-fiber milling and brushless motor integration, it must obtain a Factory Establishment Permit under the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act before commencing construction or installing production machinery. The application must describe the manufacturing process, CNC milling machines, motor winding and balancing equipment, dust collection systems, carbon-fiber prepreg storage, lithium battery charging area, and waste storage. The local government will review the site against the National Land Planning and Utilization Act, the Building Act, and local zoning ordinances. If the factory is located inside an industrial estate, KICOX coordinates the approval; if outside, the municipal authority consults with the fire, environment, and labor departments. The permit may impose conditions on noise, dust, and hazardous substance handling. The factory cannot begin operations until the completion confirmation inspection is passed and the occupancy permit is issued.
required_dossiers: Factory establishment application form
Manufacturing process flow diagram and machine list
Factory floor plan and site plan signed by a licensed architect
Building lease or ownership certificate and cadastral map
Carbon-fiber dust and hazardous materials management plan
Fire protection diagram and structural load calculations
Environmental consultation and discharge pre-review documents
Certificate of corporate signatory authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit application is rejected or suspended, request a pre-consultation with the municipal or KICOX office, amend the drawings and environmental plans, resubmit within 30 days, or file an administrative appeal under the Administrative Litigation Act. Judicial appeal to the competent administrative court is available after administrative review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Impact Assessment, Civil Defense Fire Safety, and Product Safety (KC) Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Ministry of Environment office, National Fire Agency, local Civil Defense control authority, and Korea Agency for Technology and Standards (KATS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a physical factory processing carbon fiber and assembling battery-powered FPV racing drones, the operator must complete the applicable environmental assessment procedure before operation. Depending on the factory floor area and pollutant emissions, the company must file an environmental registration or a prior environmental review, or prepare a full environmental impact assessment if the site exceeds the statutory thresholds or is located in an ecologically sensitive area. The fire fighting systems must be designed, installed, inspected, and certified under the Firefighting Systems Installation and Maintenance Act. The civil defense authority may require an emergency preparedness plan and civil defense shelter designation for the factory. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the company must complete a risk assessment for dust explosion hazards and lithium battery fire risk. KATS requires KC safety certification or safety confirmation for FPV drones sold as toys or household hobby articles, including battery and charger safety, electromagnetic compatibility, and mandatory Korean warning labels.
required_dossiers: Environmental impact assessment or prior environmental review report
Wastewater, air emissions, and hazardous waste management plans
Firefighting system design and installation completion certificates
Civil defense emergency plan and shelter assignment document
Occupational Safety and Health Act workplace risk assessment report
KC product safety test reports issued by a KATS-designated testing laboratory
Certificate of completion for dust explosion prevention equipment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the environmental agency requires supplemental data, conduct additional dispersion and dust modeling, install enhanced filters, and resubmit the revised report. If the fire safety certificate is withheld, correct the documented deficiencies with a licensed fire-fighting equipment contractor and request reinspection within 14 days. If KC certification fails, amend the product design and labeling and apply for retesting with the same or another designated laboratory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Industrial Complex Corporation (KICOX); local Si/Gun/Gu municipal government for Factory Establishment Permit and building occupancy; National Tax Service for the Business Registration Certificate; Korea Agency for Technology and Standards (KATS) for KC product safety certification.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Establishment Permit under the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act; Business Registration Certificate under the Framework Act on National Taxes; KC Safety Certification under the Electrical and Household Products Safety Control Act and the Safety Control of Children's Products Act for FPV racing/hobby drones sold as toys, including lithium battery and charger safety requirements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, through its regional environmental branch office, together with the local Si/Gun/Gu environmental department and the Korea Environment Corporation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - Environmental Registration and Prior Environmental Review for small to medium-sized carbon-fiber milling and motor assembly factories; Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report only where the factory development area exceeds the statutory thresholds under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, generally 30,000 square meters or more for manufacturing facilities, or where the site lies in an ecologically sensitive zone. At a minimum, environmental registration with the local municipality and Clean Air Conservation Act and Water Environment Conservation Act permits are mandatory before operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For the permitted manufacturing facility: wastewater discharged from the factory boundary must meet pH 5.8-8.6, BOD 25 mg/L or less, COD 40 mg/L or less, suspended solids 25 mg/L or less, total nitrogen 20 mg/L or less, and total phosphorus 2.0 mg/L or less. Airborne volatile organic compounds (VOCs) at the factory property boundary must not exceed 20 ppm as carbon for milling and coating areas under the local air preservation ordinance. Carbon-fiber particulate matter in the workplace air must not exceed 10 mg/m3, with local exhaust ventilation and dust collection systems designed to maintain compliance with occupational exposure limits. Hazardous wastes including resin-contaminated carbon-fiber offcuts, spent lithium cells, and coolant fluids must be segregated in licensed storage and removed by a licensed waste carrier under manifest documentation within 180 days of accumulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Fighting Systems Installation Completion Certificate and periodic Fire Safety Inspection Certificate issued by the National Fire Agency; Civil Defense emergency preparedness and shelter assignment approval from the local civil defense authority; structural load inspection certificate by a licensed Korean architect for CNC milling machinery vibration and roof-mounted dust extraction equipment; and Occupational Safety and Health Act workplace safety approval covering dust explosion prevention, local exhaust ventilation, emergency exits, lithium battery fire suppression, and annual risk assessments. These clearances are statutory pre-operation conditions and must be maintained and renewed according to the applicable inspection intervals.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, administered through the HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr). Export customs clearance is administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa (Korean LLC), the registration procedure begins with judicial/company registration under the Korean Commercial Act at the competent court registry. After registration and before commencing taxable commercial activity, the company must file the statutory Application for Business Registration with the district tax office having jurisdiction over its registered domestic place of business. The application must be accompanied by the certified corporate registry extract, articles of incorporation, shareholder and beneficial owner identification, proof of the domestic place of business, representative identification, and, where applicable, a foreign-investment report filed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The NTS then verifies the business establishment and issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as both the corporate Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the VAT registration number. The company must subsequently register for the NTS HomeTax electronic tax invoice system. For a non-resident foreign entity with Korean VAT obligations but no domestic permanent establishment, a separate non-resident tax registration procedure applies, requiring appointment of a Korean tax representative and registration with the NTS under the relevant provisions of the Value-Added Tax Act and Framework Act on National Taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election or a pass-through entity election for Yuhan Hoesa companies. A Korean LLC is mandatorily treated as a separate entity-level taxpayer. No hybrid-mismatch entity classification election exists under Korean corporate income tax law. The only related elective regime is the consolidated corporate tax return election available to a parent corporation with a wholly-owned domestic subsidiary group, which does not alter the separate taxable status of the LLC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No corporate turnover threshold applies to a Yuhan Hoesa company. A Korean corporation is a general VAT taxpayer and must register as soon as it commences business, regardless of projected revenue, because the simplified taxable-person regime is available only to certain individual businesses whose annual taxable supplies do not exceed KRW 80,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices must be issued as electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax electronic tax invoice system or through NTS-certified third-party software integrated via the official HomeTax API/EDI interface with an NTS-issued digital authentication certificate. Invoice data must be transmitted to the NTS by the day following the date of supply. Korea does not operate a pre-clearance fiscal-stamping model; instead, anti-fraud controls rely on centralized electronic invoice matching, mandatory linkage between export declarations, VAT returns, and customs clearance data, plus NTS risk-based real-time audit selection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, zero rating for exports of goods applies when the FPV racing drones are sold to a non-resident buyer, the goods are physically exported from Korea under a customs export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS, ownership and risk pass to the foreign buyer, and the export proceeds are settled in foreign currency through a Korean foreign exchange bank in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Qualifying offshore services, including certain digital supplies delivered and used outside Korea, may also be zero rated where the Korean VAT place-of-supply rules place the supply abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS, including the export declaration number and export clearance certificate
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or multimodal transport document evidencing shipment to the non-resident buyer and foreign destination port
Commercial Invoice containing the zero-rated export notation and product description for FPV drones
Export sales contract or irrevocable purchase order from the non-resident buyer evidencing the foreign trade transaction

Bank-issued Foreign Exchange Receipt Certificate, Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC), or functional equivalent issued under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act evidencing actual repatriation of export proceeds
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice issued through the NTS HomeTax system with the export declaration reference recorded in the prescribed zero-rating field
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS systematically cross-matches electronic tax invoice data, Korea Customs Service export declarations, transportation records, and bank foreign-exchange receipts. If any mandatory document is missing or inconsistent, the claimed zero rating is rejected and the supply is reclassified as a domestic taxable supply, resulting in assessment of VAT at 10% plus statutory interest and surtaxes. Deliberate or dishonest export zero-rating claims are subject to additional penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act, including surcharges up to 40% of the understated tax for fraudulent reporting, mandatory clawback of any refunded VAT with interest, and criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act for serious cases of false refund fraud. The ordinary statutory statute of limitations for VAT assessment is generally five years from the relevant filing deadline, with extended time limits for fraudulent or non-filed returns.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a largely liberalised current account while maintaining a controlled yet investment-friendly capital account. The Korean won is freely convertible for underlying trade, dividends, profits, and service-related inflows/outflows; however, all cross-border transfers exceeding USD 50,000 equivalent must be routed through a domestic foreign exchange bank and a supporting statutory declaration (e.g., Form FD-TR) may be required. Capital account convertibility requires prior registration with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Bank of Korea for equity investment, loans, and financial derivatives. Non-resident shareholders may remit after-tax profits without incremental approval provided the capital was legally imported and the entity complied with quarterly corporate tax filings. A foreign investor establishing a Yuhan Hoesa must file a 'Foreign Direct Investment Report' with MOEF (via a local bank) before injecting share capital in order to secure the tax benefits and ensure outward remittance rights. In practice, the bank scrutinizes high volumes of same-day in/out flows and can defer conversion if suspicious. Surrender requirements for export proceeds were abolished in 2020, but exporters are required to report inward receipts to an authorised bank within 15 business days and settle records with the Korea Customs Service. Overall, convertibility is high for ordinary trade but subject to documentary evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 6-3 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be received within six (6) months from the date of export declaration; an extension may be granted by the foreign exchange bank for cause. The exporter has no statutory obligation to convert proceeds into KRW; proceeds may be held in a domestic foreign currency account (FE-account) or sold at the prevailing market rate. However, any receipt must be brought into the Korean banking system within fifteen (15) business days of the export invoice settlement date and recorded in an FX monitoring statement. If the company does not repatriate within the six-month limit, it must file an explanatory report with the designated bank and the Korea Customs Service to avoid a foreign-exchange violation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) + Foreign Currency USD Account
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) + Foreign Currency USD E-commerce Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Direct Investment Deposit) + FX Treasury Line
Capital Escrow Account + Trade Finance LC / Collection Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Under the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, non-bank fintech EMI providers are not permitted to execute foreign exchange settlements, open operating accounts for corporate entities, or deliver cross-border payments on behalf of Korean resident companies. Only banks licensed to deal in foreign exchange by MOEF can perform such services. Global fintechs such as Revolut or Wise may offer ancillary payment initiation or money transfer services to individuals, but legally they cannot act as the primary clearing bank or FX counterparty for a Korean LLC. Thus the entity is advised to use a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank for all regulated FX flows, with PayPal/Stripe operating solely as the front-end merchant aggregator that ultimately settles to the domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory representative must appear in-branch in Korea for the initial account opening and for any subsequent signing of foreign exchange hedging documentation. Remote video verification is acceptable only for a non-resident director when the Korean resident director also appears in person, and the non-resident executes a notarized power of attorney apostilled by the Korean consulate. All directors, shareholders exercising control, and senior financial officers (if any) must provide certified passport copies, proof of address, and a beneficial ownership declaration. Physical presence of at least one natural person director with a Korean residence or temporary visa (D-7, D-8, E-2) is mandatory to satisfy the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) requirements under the Korean Special Act on Financial Information and Anti-Money Laundering.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership structure with a 100% non-resident sole shareholder and no local office, creating a shell-company risk rating.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized shareholder register and apostilled parent-company certificate, Korean Business Registration Certificate or comparable regulatory filing, the resident director's Alien Registration Card and lease agreement for a physical office, a one-year business plan with inventory storage details, and a completed beneficial ownership transparency form signed by all qualifying shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use product concern: FPV drone components may be treated as unmanned aerial vehicle parts potentially subject to export control or sanctions screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed technical specifications proving hobby-racing classification (e.g., 5-inch class carbon-fiber frame, 1400KV brushless motor, no autonomous GPS or payload capability), end-user certification for all direct buyers, a letter of non-restricted product status from the Korea Strategic Trade Institute (KOSTI), and international export control classification (ECCN) confirmation, if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk e-commerce payment routing via PayPal and Stripe with incoming customer funds classified as card-not-present or remote origin, obscuring the underlying trade invoice trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PSP merchant agreement for each payment service provider, monthly aggregated settlement statements from PayPal/Stripe backed by the bank's own API feed, order-level reconciliation showing invoice number, buyer ID, shipping tracking number, and product sales tax certificate; plus a copy of the e-commerce platform (Shopify/WooCommerce) backend for topology recognition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Minimal initial paid-in capital and immediate high-value import flows may be seen as front-running or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A capital escrow deposit of at least KRW 10,000,000 in the company's name at the opening bank, a Korean CPA-prepared capital verification report, SWIFT credit confirmation evidencing the source of wealth, supplier purchase orders, import customs declarations (Korea Customs Service), and logistics carrier bills of lading.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign share capital must be wired from the non-resident shareholder's overseas account to the company's capital escrow account at a designated Korean Tier-1 commercial bank. The SWIFT MT103 must include the Bank of Korea FX purpose code for 'Foreign Direct Investment Capital' and a free-text note in field 70 reading 'YUHANGHOESA CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION - FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT DECLARATION NR.' On arrival, the bank verifies the funds against the accepted FD declaration and issues an 'Investment Deposit Confirmation' certificate. The company's auditor then produces a capital verification report confirming the stated paid-in capital, which is filed with MOEF and the local tax office.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For component suppliers, the company will use SWIFT MT103 remittances with export settlement purpose code 'Payments for Imports of Goods' and present a supplier invoice, packing list and customs declaration in each disbursement. For high-frequency consignments from suppliers in China or South-East Asia, open an irrevocable at-sight documentary L/C through Shinhan or Hana Bank, allowing the supplier to present shipping documents for financing. For sporadic or low-value imports, the company may use documentary collection D/P (documents against payment) or D/A (documents against acceptance) with the Korean bank's trade desk. All outgoing payments are capped at 30 days pre-shipment or 180 days post-shipment unless novelty approval is obtained from MOEF.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign exchange contracts (USD/KRW, EUR/KRW) for confirmed trade payables and receivables with a maximum maturity of 12 months and a single-bank ISDA/CSA (or Korea Financial Investment Association FX Master Agreement).
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY/KRW for Chinese RMB-denominated supplier payments where the offshore RMB market is restricted and settlement is net settled in KRW.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for hedging long-term foreign-currency loans or bond-like shareholder loans, subject to MOEF prior notification and to documentation under the Korean Capital Markets Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return including tax reconciliation schedules and attachable financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March immediately following a 31 December fiscal year-end; extended to 30 April if prepared and signed by a licensed tax representative
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a non-filing additional tax of 20% of the overdue corporate income tax (40% in aggravated or large-corporation cases), plus statutory daily late-payment surcharge from the day after the due date; prolonged non-filing can lead to tax liens, distraint, compulsory collection, criminal prosecution, and ex officio closure of the registered business by the district tax office once the entity is classified as dormant.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Si/Gun/Gu Local Tax Authority of the jurisdiction where the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 April for a 31 December fiscal-year-end, filed through the local government electronic tax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment attracts local additional taxes and late-payment surcharges under the Local Tax Act; non-payment can result in seizure of bank accounts and receivables, compulsory collection, and administrative closure of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Two statutory VAT filing periods: 1 January to 30 June due by 25 July; 1 July to 31 December due by 25 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a VAT return triggers a 20% non-filing additional tax and 10% unfaithful-filing additional tax in appropriate cases; overdue VAT accrues statutory daily interest surcharges; persistent non-compliance can escalate to criminal sanctions and administrative closure of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Approval at the Members' General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records and statutory minute book maintained at the registered office; no public filing is required for a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal-year-end, i.e., by 30 June for a 31 December fiscal-year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the members' meeting or to approve financial statements is a breach of the Korean Commercial Act; directors or member-managers may be subject to administrative fines; banks or counterparties may treat the failure as an event of default; it does not by itself trigger automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent CPA Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) / Korea Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA) electronic audit-report filing systems, where statutory external audit is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For statutory audit-subject companies with a 31 December fiscal-year-end, the audited financial statements must be presented to the members' meeting by 30 June and the external audit report must be filed over the statutory electronic system by the same deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or to file the audit report can result in administrative sanctions, fines, restrictions on dividend distribution, and rejection of the financial statements by tax and financial authorities; continued non-compliance may be investigated by the FSS and may result in criminal penalties, though it does not constitute automatic corporate strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a mandatory independent audit by a certified public accountant is triggered for a Yuhan Hoesa if: (1) total assets at the end of the fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000); (2) the company is listed, publicly traded, or subject to public disclosure obligations; (3) the company is a financial institution, public-interest legal entity, or designated company requiring statutory external audit; or (4) the company is consolidated into a listed parent requiring audited consolidated financial statements. For an ordinary private limited-liability Yuhan Hoesa, no standalone turnover or headcount-only audit trigger exists; the decisive general balance-sheet threshold is KRW 12 billion in total assets. The audit must be performed by an independent registered CPA and reported under the External Audit Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for listed companies and for audit-subject public-interest entities; non-listed Yuhan Hoesa companies may apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP), specifically the General Corporate Accounting Standards or the SME Accounting Standards issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board; accounting records must also comply with the Korean Commercial Act, the Corporate Tax Act, and the Framework Act on National Taxes for tax accounting purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no stand-alone annual beneficial-ownership filing to a Korean corporate registry for an ordinary private Yuhan Hoesa. Under the Financial Transaction Reports Act and anti-money-laundering rules, financial institutions and virtual asset service providers must identify and verify the beneficial owner before establishing a business relationship and must perform ongoing customer due diligence, normally reconfirming beneficial-owner information when risk profiles change or at periodic review intervals. In the event of a shareholding transfer, the transfer must be approved by the members' general meeting unless the articles of incorporation provide otherwise, the Register of Members must be updated, the relevant commercial registration must be amended at the competent registration court, and the updated beneficial-ownership details must be submitted to the company's banking and payment service providers within 30 days of the transfer. Foreign-invested companies are also required to report changes in ownership or capital within 30 days under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through KOTRA or the relevant Korean authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges, Pledges, and Encumbrances on Shares or Company Assets
Minute Book of Members' General Meetings and Directors' Meetings
Accounting Books and Source Supporting Documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - 2,500 per annum for registered-office and corporate secretarial support in Seoul; USD 500 - 1,500 per annum outside Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 20,000 per annum if statutory external audit is triggered; USD 2,500 - 7,000 for voluntary review or financial-statement preparation services in the non-audit SME range

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: National Corporate Tax Rate (KR): progressive brackets of 9% (up to KRW 200m), 19% (KRW 200m-20bn), 21% (KRW 20bn-30bn), 24% (above KRW 30bn), plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate tax assessed.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory incentives available to an FPV drone manufacturer/retailer include: the R&D tax credit under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (up to 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure depending on company size and growth phases); foreign-investment tax reductions in Free Economic Zones (35%-100% corporate tax exemption for up to 5 years for foreign-invested enterprises); small/medium enterprise tax deduction for income derived from patented technology; special cash subsidies for strategic high-tech industries under the Special Act on the Promotion of Strategic Technology.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Beob-in-se-gwa-se-pyo-jun mit Se-ae-sin-go-seo) submitted electronically via the HomeTax National Tax Service web portal (https://www.hometax.go.kr). For a standard calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, the return is Form No. 21 (Self-Assessment Corporate Tax Return and Statement of Taxable Income) with required attachments including the financial statements, tax reconciliation schedule, and transaction-related disclosure schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing, with semi-annual prepayment of corporate tax (interim quarterly estimation) due within three months of the first half of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending December 31, the final corporate income tax return must be filed and paid within 3 months of the fiscal year-end (by March 31 of the following year). Interim tax prepayments are due by August 31 for the first half-year period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business identity, legal form, ownership profile, and foreign shareholder information (including ultimate beneficial ownership of the Korean LLC).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the full name, tax identification number (if a foreign company), residence address, and percentage ownership of every non-resident shareholder. Attach a statement confirming whether any DTA claims reduce withholding on distributions. Failure to list non-resident owners may trigger anti-avoidance review and a 10% penalty surcharge on omitted reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: GAAP profit before tax from the Korean statutory accounts, before tax reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the RC racing drone enterprise, must include all export sales revenue in gross sales, adjust inventory of carbon-fiber parts and brushless motors using arm's length pricing. If the Korean entity purchases components from related overseas suppliers above market benchmark, an adjustment must be entered here; otherwise transfer pricing assessment risk increases.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit and deduction for taxes paid outside Korea by the domestic entity on foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korea entity paid withholding or income taxes abroad on sales/distribution royalties, claim credit only where the income is included in taxable income and supported by a certified foreign tax receipt. For non-resident shareholders, this section also calculates the withholding obligations on dividends paid out of after-tax profits; no foreign tax credit is available at the shareholder level on a Korean return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding taxes on non-resident interest, dividends, royalties, and other income paid by the Korean company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For every remittance to a non-resident (e.g., dividends to a foreign parent company, royalty payments for FPV control software, interest on intercompany loans), prepay or remit statutory withholding within 10 days of payment. Indicate the gross amount paid, the WHT rate applied (domestic 22% including local surtax), the reduced treaty rate, and attach the treaty relief certificate. Incomplete or late filing will result in a 3% late-withholding penalty per day for up to 30%, plus criminal liability under Article 19 of the Tax Crimes Punishment Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income as adjusted, applicable tax rate bracket, and computed national corporate tax before prepayments and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the 9% bracket only if taxable income stays below KRW 200m for the year; watch controlled-foreign-corporation income inclusions and TP adjustments that may push profit into higher brackets. In the non-resident context, if the foreign parent entity is deemed the beneficial owner of a Korean subsidiary's profits, DTA dividend relief at 5-10% may be claimed, but the Korean entity must still file at the standard rates and prove the distribution qualifies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late/non-filing: additional 20% of the undisclosed tax (unfounded omission) or 40% if fraudulent; failure to remit withheld non-resident tax: penalty of 3% per day up to 30% of unpaid WHT plus daily late-payment interest at 0.022% for other corporate assessable taxes; criminal false declaration may be prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, exposing the corporate payer to a fine up to twice the evaded amount and responsible officers to imprisonment for up to 3 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local resident surtax, resulting in a combined statutory rate of 22% on dividends paid by a Korean Yuhan Hoesa to a non-resident corporate shareholder (Article 98 of the Corporate Tax Act controlling the national withholding aspect; local surtax is imposed under the Local Tax Act).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced DTA withholding rate, the non-resident recipient must (i) submit an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence state tax authority, dated within 12 months; (ii) complete and file the 'Application for Non-Resident Tax Exemption/Reduction under Tax Treaties' through HomeTax or at the local district tax office with jurisdiction over the Korean payer; (iii) provide a notarized beneficial ownership declaration stating that the recipient has no obligation to pass on the income and meets substantive activity requirements; (iv) evidence of entitlement in cases of intermediate holding entities; (v) remit the application before or at time of payment, although a refund claim may be filed within 3 years if approved after payment. The Korean payer retains the documents for 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory combined rate 22% (20% national + 2% local); DTA rates commonly range from 10% to 15% for industrial/technological royalties (e.g., royalties for FPV drone firmware licenses). Interest: statutory combined rate 22%; DTA rates generally range from 0% (e.g., certain triangular financing) to 15%, often 10% under Korea's modern treaties. To apply a treaty rate, the beneficial owner must satisfy the same TRC and anti-abuse conditions. The statute of limitation on under-withholding deficiency is 5 normal years, or 10 years for unjustifiable non-disclosure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File requirement: where the Korean entity's applied transactions (purchases, sales, royalties, loans) with foreign related parties exceed KRW 50 billion in the fiscal year; Master File requirement: where the multinational enterprise group has consolidated annual revenue exceeding KRW 1 trillion and the Korean entity's foreign related-party transaction volume exceeds KRW 50 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies no separate Economic Substance Regulation for domestic companies, but the body of law combines the place-of-effective-management rule (a foreign company managed in Korea is Korean resident), the Controlled Foreign Corporation (CFC) regime, and the general principle that transfer pricing arrangements must reflect actual functions, assets, and risks. For an FPV drone trading vehicle, substance is evidenced by board meetings in Korea, operational control of inventory, contract negotiation, marketing decisions, and accountable service cash flows; a paper-only Korean distributor (particularly a holding in a low-tax regime) may be recharacterized as agent or deemed holding company and taxed accordingly under the Law for International Tax Adjustment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating revenue from direct-to-consumer online sales of FPV racing drones (via PayPal and Stripe payment rails) or transferring profits to a non-resident related party through inflated carbon-fiber/brushless-motor procurement invoices, without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 9 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and Article 108 of the Corporate Tax Act, the tax authority imposes a fraudulent underreporting penalty equal to 40% of the evaded national tax (plus local surcharge 10%), daily interest surcharge at 0.022%, and criminal prosecution with imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine equal to twice the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil where the Korean LLC is a sham: directors become jointly and severally liable for the tax debts and penalties; travel ban (blacklist) is automatically issued during criminal investigation; upon conviction the individual director faces civil restitution to the National Tax Service, disqualification from serving as a corporate officer for a term, and actual imprisonment for up to 3 years (aggravated to up to 10 years under the Special Act for the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes where tax evaded exceeds KRW 300 million).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a Hong Kong or zero-tax regional holding company between a foreign beneficiary and the Korean operating LLC for the purpose of channeling Korean dividends, interest, or software royalties through an entity with no office, staff, active management, or business purpose, solely to obtain a favorable DTA withholding rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean tax authority will deny treaty benefits based on the beneficial owner and principal purpose tests under the OECD-conforming rules (Law for International Tax Adjustment, Article 2-1 and Article 6). The deficiency becomes the full 22% withholding tax plus a 40% false-claim penalty; interest and charges accrue at 0.022% daily; foreign exchange controls may be applied to cross-border transfers. The penal consequences for the Korean payer include liability for uncollected WHT as withholding agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the intercompany financing, royalty, or dividend resolution are treated as responsible withholding officers; they can be personally assessed for unremitted tax, subjected to mandatory travel ban during prosecution, and prosecuted for aiding and abetting tax evasion, carrying imprisonment of 1-5 years and a fine of up to KRW 200 million (under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 18). Civil liability extends to restoring funds transferred out of the Korean entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Default / Artificial Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare, retain, or submit the Local File, Master File, and country-by-country report (if thresholds met) for cross-border drone component purchases, license arrangements, or management service fees, or submitting false functional and risk analyses that do not reflect the actual drone manufacturing activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 12 of the Law for International Tax Adjustment, failure to submit transfer pricing documentation within the request deadline triggers a KRW 50 million per-document penalty and allows the tax authority to estimate taxable income using its own benchmark methods; under-assessed tax will bear a 10% gross negligence surcharge (20% for omission without based-on-review justification) plus 0.022% daily delay interest. The National Tax Service may also impose a secondary adjustment and deem additional dividends to the foreign shareholder, subject to 22% withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for accounting and tax management may be held civilly liable for company losses caused by the fine; deliberate destruction or concealment of exchange-control and manufacturing cost records invokes criminal liability under Article 15-2 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, leading to imprisonment of up to 3 years, and a personal ban from travel overseas during any pending criminal and extradition procedures.
